artiest/paul-van-dyk.text:
Paul van Dyk is the stage name of Matthias Paul, a German DJ and producer born in 1971. He grew up in East Berlin with his single mother. His musical education came from the radio. There were few record shops, so he secretly listened to Western stations and to mixtapes that were sometimes smuggled into the country. His first album was Organisation by Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark, which he later called hugely influential. Shortly before the fall of the Wall he was allowed to travel to Hamburg with his mother. In 1990 he returned to Berlin. In March 1991 he played for the first time at the club Tresor.

His name sounds Belgian because in the beginning he played a lot of Belgian dance records. In 1993 his first mix compilation X-Mix-1 appeared and he made a remix of Humate's Love Stimulation, a trance anthem on the Berlin label MFS. The hit For an Angel followed in 1994, along with the album 45 RPM. Later came Seven Ways (1996) and Out There and Back (2000). With Reflections (2003) he was the first artist to receive a Grammy nomination in the new category of Best Dance/Electronic Album. In 2005 and 2006 DJ Magazine voted him number one in the world.

Van Dyk makes trance: melodic, driving electronic music with long build-ups. He is one of the DJs who took Berlin's post-Wall club culture to the world. His most recent albums include Music Rescues Me (2018) and This World Is Ours (2025). He also presents the radio programme VONYC Sessions.
artiest/paul-van-dyk.listen: Listen to For an Angel. Notice how the melody and the beat slowly build towards a climax, and what that does to the tension in the track.

artiest/paul-van-nevel.text:
Paul Van Nevel was born in 1946 and is a Belgian conductor, musicologist and art historian. He grew up in a musical family. From the age of eleven to eighteen he sang four hours a day, and his father, who played the violin, encouraged him to try every instrument in the house. His father loved Wagner; he himself chose Béla Bartók. From 1969 to 1971 he studied early music at the Schola Cantorum Basiliensis in Switzerland. There, in 1971, he founded the Huelgas Ensemble, a choir devoted to the polyphonic music of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance. The name comes from the Codex Las Huelgas, from a Cistercian monastery near Burgos, which he visited at the age of twenty-four and was able to study for two weeks.

Van Nevel is known for tracking down little-known medieval polyphony, which he then performs. The Huelgas Ensemble recorded, among other things, Las Ensaladas, Ars moriendi and La Favola di Orfeo. His recordings have won several prizes, including the Diapason d'Or in 1996 and the MIDEM Cannes Classical Award for best choral music in 1998. In 1994 he received the Prix Paris in honorem of the Académie Charles Cros.

He teaches at the conservatoire in Amsterdam and has been guest conductor of the Collegium Vocale Gent, the Netherlands Chamber Choir and the choir of the Netherlands Bach Society. Van Nevel is known for his love of cigars, which comes through in the 2011 album The Art of the Cigar.
artiest/paul-van-nevel.listen: Listen to a recording by the Huelgas Ensemble, for example Las Ensaladas. Notice how several voices weave through one another without any single voice carrying the melody alone.

artiest/paul-weller.text:
Paul Weller, born John William Weller, was born in 1958 in Woking, Surrey. His love of music began with the Beatles, followed by The Who and the Small Faces. He began playing guitar at eleven, and a Status Quo concert in 1972 confirmed his calling. In the late 1970s he became famous as the guitarist, singer and main songwriter of The Jam, with Bruce Foxton and Rick Buckler. The band was both a critical and a commercial success in Britain and was the most influential group of the mod revival of the late 1970s and early 1980s.

At the end of 1982 Weller disbanded The Jam and formed The Style Council with Mick Talbot. In it he tried out a wide range of styles, from pop and jazz to soul, hip hop, folk and classical. He then began a solo career, with albums such as Paul Weller (1992), Wild Wood (1993), Stanley Road (1995), Heavy Soul (1997) and later, among others, 22 Dreams (2008) and A Kind Revolution (2017).

Weller is famous above all in his own country, because his lyrics are rooted in English society. The songs of The Jam are often about working-class life. He is known as the Modfather and influenced later British alternative rock and Britpop, such as Oasis. He won four Brit Awards, including three for best British male, and in 2006 the Brit Award for Outstanding Contribution to Music.
artiest/paul-weller.listen: Listen to Wild Wood from the 1993 album of the same name. Notice the guitar and the vocals, and compare it with what you know of The Jam.

artiest/paul-wertico.text:
Paul Wertico was born in 1953 in Chicago and is an American drummer. He became known as a member of the Pat Metheny Group, from 1983 to 2001. Metheny heard the Simon & Bard Group, in which Wertico played together with the bassist Steve Rodby, and asked both for his own band. With Metheny, Wertico played on ten albums and four videos, appeared on television and toured all over the world. He won seven Grammys, including for Best Jazz Fusion Performance, Best Contemporary Jazz Performance and Best Rock Instrumental Performance. He left the group in 2001 to have more time for his family and to make other music.

Afterwards he formed the Paul Wertico Trio with John Moulder and Eric Hochberg and worked with Larry Coryell, Kurt Elling and Jeff Berlin. From 2000 to 2007 he played in SBB, a Polish progressive rock band. He played on Kurt Elling's Grammy-nominated albums Close Your Eyes and The Messenger, and on Paul Winter's Earth: Voices of a Planet. He also played with, among others, Lee Konitz, Roscoe Mitchell, Evan Parker, Mike Stern and Ramsey Lewis.

Wertico is also a teacher: he is affiliated with Roosevelt University in Chicago, taught for years at Northwestern University and gives clinics all over the world. From 2010 to 2012 he presented his own radio show about jazz, and he devised TUBZ, a drum accessory.
artiest/paul-wertico.listen: Listen to First Circle by the Pat Metheny Group, the first album with Wertico. Notice how the drums drive the music forward with shifting time signatures.

artiest/paul-whiteman.text:
Paul Whiteman was born in 1890 and was an American bandleader, composer, conductor and violinist. In the 1920s and early 1930s he led one of the most popular dance orchestras in the United States. His records sold enormously well and the press called him the King of Jazz. His best-known recordings include Whispering, Valencia, Three O'Clock in the Morning, In a Little Spanish Town and Parade of the Wooden Soldiers. He also recorded Wang Wang Blues, Mississippi Mud and Hot Lips, and in 1925 co-wrote Flamin' Mamie.

Whiteman led an unusually large ensemble and tried out many styles. He combined symphonic music with jazz, as at the premiere of George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue. His orchestra played a varied programme, from pop songs and waltzes to semi-classical works and jazz, and his bands included many of the best white musicians of the day, among them Bix Beiderbecke. In the swing era from the mid-1930s his popularity faded, and in the 1940s he was almost retired. In the 1950s he made a comeback with his own television series Paul Whiteman's Goodyear Revue.

His place in early jazz is disputed. Critics consider his richly orchestrated music jazz in name only, lacking improvisation and emotion, and point out that he took over innovations by black musicians. Historians point out that his love of jazz was genuine. Duke Ellington wrote in his autobiography that no one had worn the title King of Jazz with more certainty and dignity.
artiest/paul-whiteman.listen: Listen to Rhapsody in Blue in the recording by Whiteman's orchestra. Notice how jazz and classical music come together here.

artiest/paul-williams.text:
Paul Williams, in full David Paul Gifford Williams, is an English composer, songwriter and producer. He was born in Kingston upon Thames and began composing at the age of eight. He studied music and composition at Tiffin School and the Royal College of Music, where at twelve he was already given a Saturday-morning scholarship for talent. During his studies he worked in the summer as a pianist on the ship RMS Queen Elizabeth. He then studied at Jesus College, Cambridge, under the musicologist Thurston Dart. There he made his first professional songs and productions, including Running Shoes with the athlete Herb Elliott, which Decca released in 1964. Later David Frost invited him to the Cambridge Footlights because of his talent as a pianist.

At the BBC he worked with presenters such as Tony Blackburn and Jimmy Young. As a producer he made recordings for radio of Led Zeppelin, David Bowie and The Who. In 1969 he produced four tracks for Session 3 of Led Zeppelin's BBC Sessions, including Communication Breakdown, which came out on an album in 1997.

Williams is best known for his piano playing on production music, written for international music publishers. He writes adventurous music, romantic songs, ambient and high-tech soundscapes. This shows in the titles of his albums, such as Electric Piano Solos, Piano Moods and Piano Atmospheres.
artiest/paul-williams.listen: Listen to a piece by Williams from Piano Moods. Notice how a single piano creates an atmosphere, with no need for words or vocals.

artiest/peaches.text:
Peaches is the stage alias of Merrill Nisker, born in 1966 in Toronto, a Canadian electroclash musician and producer. Variety called her a feminist and queer icon. Before becoming a full-time musician she was a teacher. In the early 1990s she played in the folk trio Mermaid Cafe, and in 1995 she released her first solo album Fancypants Hoodlum. That same year she joined the band The Shit, with Chilly Gonzales among others. Every band member had a nickname. Hers was Peaches, taken from Nina Simone's song Four Women, in which Simone cries out at the end that her name is Peaches.

In Toronto she lived above a sex shop with her housemate Feist, who sang along at her gigs. Together they toured England from 2000 to 2001. Peaches moved to Berlin and signed with the label Kitty-Yo. The EP Lovertits came out in the summer of 2000, and the album The Teaches of Peaches followed in the autumn. It contains her best-known song, Fuck the Pain Away. Later came Fatherfucker (2003), Impeach My Bush (2006), I Feel Cream (2009) and Rub (2015).

Her music falls under electroclash. Peaches also inspired M.I.A., who started using the Roland MC-505 because of her.
artiest/peaches.listen: Listen to Fuck the Pain Away. Notice the electronic beat and the way she sings.

artiest/pearl-jam.text:
Pearl Jam is an American rock band, formed in 1990 in Seattle. The guitarist Stone Gossard and the bassist Jeff Ament started afresh with the guitarist Mike McCready after Andrew Wood, the singer of their band Mother Love Bone, died in 1990. Via the drummer Jack Irons, their demo tape ended up with Eddie Vedder, a singer from San Diego, who sang lyrics over it and sent it back. Together with Nirvana, Pearl Jam became the best-known band of the Seattle grunge scene.

The band was first called Mookie Blaylock, after a basketball player, and the debut album Ten (August 1991) is named after his jersey number. Ten sounds less raw than Nirvana. The guitars are heavy but clear, the songs long, and Vedder sings low and full. The first single, Alive, was released in July 1991. Gossard had written the music as an instrumental piece back in 1990; Vedder wrote a partly autobiographical lyric for it, about a boy who discovers that his father is in fact his stepfather. Ten spent almost five years on the American album chart and peaked at number 2. Its successor Vs. (1993) sold more than 950,000 copies in its first week, a record at the time.

Pearl Jam stood closer to the rock of the 1970s than other grunge bands. In 1994 the group filed a complaint with the American Department of Justice against the ticket seller Ticketmaster, in order to keep service fees low for fans. The investigation came to nothing. In 2017 Pearl Jam was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, in the first year it was eligible.
artiest/pearl-jam.listen: Listen to the end of Alive: after the last chorus Mike McCready takes over with a long, melodic guitar solo, as rock bands did in the 1970s. McCready has said that he borrowed that solo largely from Ace Frehley of Kiss.

artiest/peggy-lee.text:
Peggy Lee was born in 1920 as Norma Deloris Egstrom in Jamestown, North Dakota, in a family of Swedish and Norwegian descent. Her mother died when she was four. She began as a singer on local radio and then joined the big band of Benny Goodman. She built up a refined image and also wrote music for films, acted in films herself and recorded concept albums in which poetry and music came together. Her career spanned seven decades. She recorded more than 1,100 masters and co-wrote more than 270 songs.

She recorded her best-known hits for Capitol Records: Why Don't You Do Right? in 1943, Fever in 1958 and Is That All There Is? in 1969. The last two earned her a Grammy. Albums from those years include Black Coffee With Peggy Lee (1953), Dream Street (1957) and Jump for Joy (1958). Towards the end of her career she chose pure vocal jazz, for example on Miss Peggy Lee Sings the Blues from 1988.

Lee is also known for Disney's Lady and the Tramp, in which she spoke and sang the parts of Darling, Peg and the Siamese cats, among others. For her role in Pete Kelly's Blues she received an Oscar nomination in 1956. She died in 2002.
artiest/peggy-lee.listen: Listen to Fever and notice Lee's singing. Try to hear how restrained and controlled she sounds.

artiest/pepe-de-lucia.text:
Pepe de Lucía was born in 1945 as José Sánchez Gómez in Algeciras, in the Spanish province of Cádiz, and is a flamenco singer and songwriter. He is the son of the flamenco guitarist Antonio Sánchez Pecino and the brother of the guitarists Paco de Lucía and Ramón de Algeciras. He chose his stage name in honour of his Portuguese mother, Lúcia Gomes. He is the father of the Spanish pop singer Malú, and his son José de Lucía is also a flamenco musician.

He made his first record, Los Chiquitos de Algeciras, with his brother Paco. Until 1988 he sang on Paco de Lucía's albums, when Duquende replaced him. Later came albums of his own such as Caminando (1983), El orgullo de mi padre (1996), Cada día (2000) and El corazón de mi gente (2002).

Pepe de Lucía wrote many of the lyrics that Camarón de la Isla sang on his albums with Paco de Lucía and Tomatito. One example is Sentao en el Valle on the album Como el Agua.
artiest/pepe-de-lucia.listen: Listen to Sentao en el Valle by Camarón de la Isla on Como el Agua. Notice the lyrics that Pepe de Lucía wrote and how the singing and the guitar follow each other.

artiest/per-gessle.text:
Per Gessle was born in 1959 and is a Swedish singer, songwriter and guitarist. He is best known as the male half and main songwriter of the pop duo Roxette, which he founded in 1986 with Marie Fredriksson and which ceased to exist after her death in 2019. Before that he had success in Sweden as the frontman of Gyllene Tider, a group he co-founded in 1976. That group quickly became popular, but after the disappointing fourth album The Heartland Café from 1984 it broke up.

Roxette broke through internationally at the end of the 1980s and the start of the 1990s, with the albums Look Sharp! (1988) and Joyride (1991). The duo topped the American chart four times, above all with It Must Have Been Love, which was heard in the film Pretty Woman.

Besides his work with Roxette and Gyllene Tider, Gessle made many solo albums, in Swedish and in English. His first solo album Per Gessle appeared in 1982, followed by Scener in 1985. After Fredriksson's illness he released Mazarin (2003), a success with critics and public, and then Son of a Plumber (2005), En händig man (2007) and Party Crasher (2008). Later came En vacker natt, En vacker dag and Small Town Talk. Under the pseudonym Mono Mind he released the album Mind Control in 2019.
artiest/per-gessle.listen: Listen to It Must Have Been Love by Roxette. Notice the melody and the chorus.

artiest/percy-heath.text:
Percy Heath was born in 1923 in Wilmington, North Carolina, and grew up in Philadelphia. He was an American jazz bassist and the brother of the saxophonist Jimmy Heath and the drummer Albert Heath. His father played clarinet and his mother sang in the church choir. Percy began on violin at the age of eight. In 1944 he joined the army and trained with the Tuskegee Airmen, where he graduated as a second lieutenant and pilot, although he never saw action. After the war he chose music, bought a double bass and attended the Granoff School of Music in Philadelphia. Before long he was playing in the city's jazz clubs with leading musicians.

In the late 1940s he moved to New York, and he and his brother Jimmy worked in the groups of Dizzy Gillespie. Members of Gillespie's big band, among them the pianist John Lewis, the drummer Kenny Clarke and the vibraphonist Milt Jackson, decided there to form a permanent group. When the bassist Ray Brown left, Heath joined, and in 1952 the Modern Jazz Quartet officially began, with Connie Kay replacing Clarke from 1955. The quartet played until 1974, reunited in 1981 and recorded for the last time in 1993.

Heath also played with Miles Davis, Charlie Parker, Wes Montgomery, Thelonious Monk and Lee Konitz. In 1975 he formed the Heath Brothers with his brothers and the pianist Stanley Cowell. There he sometimes played cello instead of bass. He died in 2005.
artiest/percy-heath.listen: Listen to a recording by the Modern Jazz Quartet and focus on the bass. Try to hear how Heath carries the music.

artiest/perez-prado.text:
Dámaso Pérez Prado was born in 1916 in Matanzas, Cuba, the son of a teacher and a journalist. As a child he studied classical piano and later played organ and piano in local clubs. For a time he was pianist and arranger of the Sonora Matancera, Cuba's best-known dance group. He then founded his own group and in 1946 recorded in Havana, among other things, Trompetiana, a mambo of his own composition and one of the first arranged for big band. He then moved to Mexico, where he developed the genre in several forms.

His 1949 recordings, including Mambo No. 5, won him a contract with RCA Victor in the United States and an eventful career in the 1950s. He was nicknamed the King of the Mambo. In 1955 his mambo arrangement of Cherry Pink and Apple Blossom White topped the charts in the United States and England. In 1958 came Guaglione and his own Patricia. His music was also heard in films, including La Dolce Vita. In the 1960s his popularity faded because of new Latin dances such as pachanga and boogaloo. He returned to Mexico in the 1970s, became a citizen there in 1980 and died there in 1989.

Prado combined the Cuban danzón with the power of a large big band. He used fierce brass, sharp rhythms and short cries, with which the mambo became a worldwide dance. His son still leads the orchestra.
artiest/perez-prado.listen: Listen to Mambo No. 5 by Pérez Prado. Notice the sharp brass trading off with each other and the short cries between the rhythms.

artiest/perfume.text:
Perfume is a Japanese girl group made up of Nocchi, Kashiyuka and A-chan. They began in 2000 in Hiroshima, where they found each other as pupils at a talent school. Three years later they moved to Tokyo and joined the management agency Amuse. There they worked with the producer Yasutaka Nakata, who devised a technopop identity for the group. The name Perfume, Japanese for fragrance, refers to a character that appeared in the names of the first members. The idea behind it is that a scent can calm feelings or make people happy, and that the group wants to do the same.

After a series of indie singles, Perfume made its major-label debut in 2005 with Linear Motor Girl. The first records sold modestly, but in 2007 the breakthrough followed with the single Polyrhythm. The 2008 debut album Game was the start of a run of nine consecutive number-one albums. Then came, among others, Triangle (2009), JPN (2011) and Level3 (2013). In 2012 the group signed with Universal Music Group to reach a larger audience abroad as well.

The early music has a sound that derives from Shibuya-kei. Later the group moved towards contemporary electronic dance music, with elements of bitpop, techno and house. The voices are heavily processed with Auto-Tune and vocoders. Their performances stand out for the choreography and the futuristic imagery. For pop history, Perfume shows how Japanese technopop, with dance steps and electronics, could win a large audience. In 2024 and 2025 the two-part album Nebula Romance was released, for the group's twenty-fifth anniversary.
artiest/perfume.listen: Listen to Polyrhythm. Notice the processed, almost robotic voices and how the electronic rhythms interlock beneath the vocals.

artiest/perotin.text: Pérotin worked around 1200 in Paris, in the years when Notre-Dame cathedral was being built. We know almost nothing about his life; we know his name from an English treatise written half a century later. He had three or four voices sing above a greatly extended Gregorian melody, in fixed, dancing rhythms. His Viderunt omnes, probably for Christmas 1198, is one of the oldest four-voice pieces in European music.
artiest/perotin.listen: Listen to the long, sustained notes in the lowest voice and hear how three voices above them move in the same skipping rhythm.

artiest/perry-bradford.text:
Perry Bradford was born in 1893 in Montgomery, Alabama, and grew up in Atlanta. He was a composer, songwriter and vaudeville performer, nicknamed Mule for his stubbornness. In 1906 he worked in minstrel shows, and in 1909 he was already playing as a solo pianist in Chicago. As a pianist, singer, dancer and composer he travelled the theatres of the South and the North between 1908 and 1919, in a song-and-dance act under the name Bradford and Jeanette.

In New York he managed to convince Frederick W. Hager of Okeh Records to record Mamie Smith. He became her musical director, and she played the lead in his 1918 show Made in Harlem. In this way Smith became, in 1920, the first African American blues singer on record, with his song Crazy Blues. He also organised the first recording session, That Thing Called Love, in which an African American artist with a white studio band played material that belonged to African American culture.

Between 1923 and 1927 Bradford himself recorded seven sessions, with, among others, Johnny Dunn, Bubber Miley, Buster Bailey, James P. Johnson and, in 1925, Louis Armstrong on two tracks. Because of the stock market crash of 1929 and the change in jazz and African American songs, he lost influence, and during the Depression he was almost forgotten. In 1957 Little Richard had a hit with his Keep A-Knockin'. His autobiography Born With the Blues appeared in 1965.
artiest/perry-bradford.listen: Listen to Crazy Blues in the performance by Mamie Smith. Notice the singing and how a blues record from 1920 sounds.

artiest/perry-farrell.text:
Perry Farrell, born Peretz Bernstein in 1959 in Queens, New York, is an American singer, songwriter and musician. At seventeen he travelled by bus to California, with a surfboard and drawing materials, and in Los Angeles in the early 1980s he became the singer of the post-punk and gothic band Psi Com. There he used the name Perry Farrell for the first time. In 1985 he formed the band Jane's Addiction with the bassist Eric Avery, the drummer Stephen Perkins and the guitarist Dave Navarro.

Jane's Addiction became popular in Los Angeles and then in the United States with energetic performances in small venues. The group released three albums in quick succession: Jane's Addiction, Nothing's Shocking and Ritual de lo Habitual. It mixed punk, metal and psychedelic rock and became a key name in the Los Angeles scene of the 1980s. Farrell was nicknamed the Godfather of Alternative Music.

For Jane's Addiction's farewell tour in 1991, Farrell founded Lollapalooza, which grew into an annual multi-genre festival. He then formed Porno for Pyros with Perkins. Their first album from 1993 reached number three on the Billboard 200. In 2001 his first solo album Song Yet to Be Sung appeared. He also started projects such as Satellite Party and Kind Heaven Orchestra, and released Kind Heaven in 2019.
artiest/perry-farrell.listen: Listen to a track by Jane's Addiction, for example from Nothing's Shocking. Notice Farrell's singing and how punk, metal and psychedelic rock run together.

artiest/perturbator.text:
Perturbator is the stage name of James Kent, a French electronic musician from Paris, born in 1993. His parents were music journalists, and had had a band themselves in their youth. That sparked his interest in synthesizers. Before starting Perturbator he played guitar in several black metal bands.

Since 2012 he has made electronic music inspired by cyberpunk culture and films such as Akira, Ghost in the Shell and The Running Man. He uses software synthesizers that imitate classic instruments such as the OB-X and the CS-80. His first EP was called Night Driving Avenger. Later releases included I Am the Night (2012), Dangerous Days (2014), The Uncanny Valley (2016) and Lustful Sacraments (2021), often on the label Blood Music. Future Club, the track from the course, is on Dangerous Days from 2014. A mix of darkness, dark synthesizers and a hefty dose of nostalgia defines his sound. It falls under synthwave, the style that revives the electronic film music of the 1980s.

Many people got to know his music through the computer game Hotline Miami from 2012 and its 2015 sequel, in which several of his tracks are heard. This brought him a larger audience. In 2019 he appeared in the documentary The Rise of the Synths, alongside other composers from the scene and the director John Carpenter, who told the story. He has a label of his own, Music of the Void, and a side project called Ruin Of Romantics.
artiest/perturbator.listen: Listen to Future Club. Notice the dark synthesizer sounds and the tight beat, and ask yourself whether this sounds like music for a night-time drive through the city in a film.

artiest/pet-shop-boys.text:
Pet Shop Boys are an English synth-pop duo from London, formed in 1981 by the singer Neil Tennant and the keyboard player Chris Lowe. They met that year in a hi-fi shop in Chelsea and shared a love of disco and electronic music. Their early sound came from Hi-NRG, fast electronic disco music, and from the hip hop then emerging in New York.

The breakthrough was West End Girls, first released in 1984 with the producer Bobby Orlando. A new recording with the producer Stephen Hague reached number 1 in England in January 1986 and later in America too. After the debut album Please (1986) came Actually (1987), with It's a Sin, which reached number 1 in 1987. Their version of Always on My Mind and the song Heart (1988) also reached the top spot. With Dusty Springfield they made What Have I Done to Deserve This?, which revived her career.

The duo sold more than a hundred million records and in 1999 were named by the Guinness Book of Records the most successful duo in British music history. They won three Brit Awards and in 2009 received the award for their contribution to music. Their only number 1 album in England was Very (1993). The foundation remained synth-pop and dance pop, but over the years they also took in house, trance and orchestral sounds. In It's a Sin, Tennant drew on memories of his schooldays, and so it became one of the songs in which the experience of gay young people in the 1980s could be heard.
artiest/pet-shop-boys.listen: In It's a Sin, listen to the heavy, bombastic synthesizer chords and orchestra hits, which sound like a church full of reverb. Notice the moment halfway through when a Latin prayer of confession is recited in the background.

artiest/pete-bellotte.text:
Pete Bellotte is an English songwriter and producer, born in 1943 in Barnet, near London. He began as a guitarist in the group Linda Laine and the Sinners and toured Germany with them. He learned fluent German, moved to Munich and became assistant to the producer Giorgio Moroder. In 1971 he wrote the lyrics for Moroder's Son of My Father, which became a number 1 hit in England for Chicory Tip.

With Moroder, Bellotte wrote and produced the hits of Donna Summer, such as Love to Love You Baby (1975), I Feel Love (1977) and Hot Stuff (1979). The three of them also made the album I Remember Yesterday, which contains I Feel Love: a track that is almost entirely electronic, with a pulsing synthesizer bass and a tight beat. According to a critic at AllMusic, Bellotte's productions helped shape disco. He also worked with Roberta Kelly, with Sugar Cane, who had a disco hit in 1978 with Montego Bay, and with Elton John, for whose album Victim of Love (1979) he wrote songs. In 1978 and 1979 he was named producer of the year in America.

When the mood in America turned and the slogan Disco sucks went around, Bellotte became disillusioned. He returned to England and has lived in West Sussex since 1993. In 2004 he was inducted into the Dance Music Hall of Fame, and in 2012 I Feel Love was added to the National Recording Registry of the American Library of Congress.
artiest/pete-bellotte.listen: In I Feel Love, listen to the bass line: a fast, pulsing synthesizer pattern that continues throughout the track and is almost hypnotic. Notice how Donna Summer's high, floating voice drifts above it.

artiest/pete-best.text:
Pete Best was the drummer of the Beatles from 1960 to 1962. He was born in 1941 in Madras, in British India, and grew up in Liverpool. His mother, Mona Best, ran the Casbah Coffee Club in the basement of the family home, where the group, then still The Quarrymen, gave early performances. In August 1960, just before their first run of performances in Hamburg, the Beatles asked him to be their regular drummer.

In Hamburg the band played in several clubs, until the members were expelled from the country at the end of November 1960. In January 1962 they auditioned for Decca but were turned down. Later that year they ended up at EMI, where the producer George Martin felt that Best's timing was not good enough for the studio and preferred to use a session drummer. In August 1962 the manager Brian Epstein dismissed him, and Ringo Starr took his place. Various stories exist about the reasons: criticism of his drumming, relations within the band, quarrels between his mother and Epstein, and his popularity with the fans.

After the Beatles, Best played in other groups without much success. He stopped playing music for about twenty years and worked as a civil servant in Liverpool. In 1988 he started the Pete Best Band. In 1995 he received a substantial sum from the sales of Anthology 1, which contains ten tracks on which he drums. John Lennon later said that the group had behaved cowardly over his dismissal. In 2025 Best stopped performing.
artiest/pete-best.listen: On Anthology 1, listen to one of the recordings with Pete Best, such as the early version of Love Me Do from 1962, and compare it with the well-known single. Notice the drums: can you hear a difference in tempo and steadiness?

artiest/pete-burns.text:
Pete Burns was born in 1959 in Port Sunlight, in the English region of the Wirral, and was a singer, songwriter and television personality. Between 1977 and 1984 he worked as a shop assistant at Probe Records in Liverpool, where the owner hired him for his striking appearance. In 1977 he formed the punk band The Mystery Girls with Julian Cope and Pete Wylie, which gave only one performance. In 1979 came Nightmares in Wax, and in 1980 he founded Dead or Alive, of which he became lead singer. The band belonged to new wave.

The greatest success came in 1985 with You Spin Me Round (Like a Record), their first number one in Great Britain. Dead or Alive had seven British top 40 singles, two American top 20 singles and two songs that reached number one on the American dance and club chart. According to Billboard magazine, in 2016 the band was among the most successful dance artists ever. Burns also released solo records and appeared in television programmes, such as Celebrity Big Brother.

Burns stood out for his powerful, deep baritone voice and his flamboyant clothing, with an eyepatch and an androgynous look. He was called a gay icon, although he did not want to label himself. In this way he helped bring gay culture to the foreground in pop music. He died in 2016.
artiest/pete-burns.listen: Listen to You Spin Me Round (Like a Record) and notice Burns's deep voice. Try to hear how that baritone singing fits a fast, danceable rhythm.

artiest/pete-carpenter.text:
Clarence Edward Carpenter, known as Pete Carpenter, was born in 1914 and was an American jazz trombonist, arranger and composer of television themes. After a long career as a trombonist in bands and as a studio musician, he began writing music for television with the composer Earle Hagen, for series such as Bewitched, Gomer Pyle, U.S.M.C. and The Andy Griffith Show.

In 1968 his collaboration with the much younger composer Mike Post began, which lasted until his death in 1987. Their first success was the theme for Toma from 1973, the first series by the producer Stephen J. Cannell. The big breakthrough came in 1974 with the theme for The Rockford Files, starring James Garner. It became a hit in the American top ten and won a Grammy for best arrangement. Together Carpenter and Post wrote music for more than 1,800 hours of television. This includes Baa Baa Black Sheep, CHiPs, Magnum, P.I., The A-Team, Hardcastle and McCormick, Riptide, Hunter and Stingray. They also made music for films, including Vanishing Point from 1971. For Hunter they received a BMI TV Music Award in 1989.

Carpenter came from the big band world, and you can hear that experience in the themes that viewers heard every week.
artiest/pete-carpenter.listen: Listen to the theme of The A-Team. Notice how in a few seconds a recognisable melody and a march-like rhythm set the mood of the series.

artiest/pete-johnson.text:
Pete Johnson was born in 1904 in Kansas City, Missouri, and was an American boogie-woogie and jazz pianist. His father left the family, and Pete was raised by his mother. At twelve he looked for work in a factory, a printing works and as a shoeshine boy, and he left school in fifth grade. In 1922 he began his musical career as a drummer in Kansas City. Around the same time he learned piano, at first in a church. From 1926 to 1938 he worked as a pianist, often with the singer Big Joe Turner.

In 1936 a meeting with the producer John Hammond led to a performance at the Famous Door in New York, and in 1938 Johnson and Turner played in the concert From Spirituals to Swing at Carnegie Hall. After that, boogie-woogie quickly gained popularity. Johnson played and recorded with Turner, Meade Lux Lewis and Albert Ammons, the three known as the Boogie Woogie Trio. The song Roll 'Em Pete from 1938, made by Johnson and Turner, is regarded as one of the first rock 'n' roll records. In 1948 he wrote Rocket Boogie 88 with Jack Lauderdale, an instrumental that influenced Ike Turner's Rocket 88 from 1951.

According to Scott Yanow, Johnson was one of the three great boogie-woogie pianists. He was better at playing in a band than Lewis, and as an accompanist he could shine without drowning out his singer. He died in 1967.
artiest/pete-johnson.listen: Listen to Roll 'Em Pete by Pete Johnson and Big Joe Turner. Notice the rhythm of the piano and how Turner sings over it.

artiest/pete-johnson-en-big-joe-turner.text:
Pete Johnson and Big Joe Turner were a duo from Kansas City. Johnson played piano, Turner sang. Turner, born in 1911, left school at fourteen and worked in the city's nightclubs, first as a cook and later as a singing bartender. That earned him the nickname The Singing Barman. In clubs such as the Sunset he often performed with his friend Johnson. In those days Kansas City's clubs were regularly visited by the police, but after the inspection the party simply carried on until morning.

In 1936 the two went to New York, but the city was not yet ready for them. In 1938 the talent scout John Hammond saw them and invited them to one of his concerts From Spirituals to Swing at Carnegie Hall, which brought jazz and blues to a wider American audience. Their great success followed: Roll 'Em Pete, in fact a collection of traditional blues lyrics. Turner often re-recorded the song in the years afterwards. In 1939 they played with the boogie-woogie pianists Albert Ammons and Meade Lux Lewis at Café Society in New York, on the same bill as Billie Holiday.

Turner was known as a blues shouter: a singer with a powerful voice who could rise above a band. His greatest fame came in the 1950s with rock 'n' roll recordings such as Shake, Rattle and Roll. In 1987 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Roll 'Em Pete shows how boogie-woogie and blues prepared the way for rock 'n' roll.
artiest/pete-johnson-en-big-joe-turner.listen: Listen to Roll 'Em Pete. Notice Turner's powerful singing and how the pianist's left hand plays a continuously rolling pattern.

artiest/pete-rock-en-c-l-smooth.text:
Pete Rock & CL Smooth were an American hip hop duo from Mount Vernon, New York. Pete Rock, real name Peter Phillips, and CL Smooth, Corey Penn, met at Mount Vernon High School. They sent demos to labels, until Elektra Records offered them a production deal via the management company The Untouchables, with DJ Eddie F. On 25 June 1991 their first EP, All Souled Out, was released. In 1992 came their debut album Mecca and the Soul Brother, and in 1994 the second album The Main Ingredient.

Pete Rock made his name as a producer and DJ through his use of obscure soul and jazz records, often with a horn riff as the hook. CL Smooth rapped in a more conscious tone, which stood apart from the gangsta rap of the time. He mostly avoided swearing and resembled, in style and delivery, the positive East Coast rappers such as those in the Native Tongues Crew. Their best-known hit is They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.), a requiem for fallen friends, in particular Troy Dixon, nicknamed Trouble T-Roy, a member of Heavy D & The Boyz, who died in 1990.

The duo split up. In 2011 Pete Rock said that a new album was in the making, the third and the first since 1994.
artiest/pete-rock-en-c-l-smooth.listen: Listen to They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.). Notice the soul and jazz samples on which the track rests, and CL Smooth's conscious, calm delivery.

artiest/pete-rugolo.text:
Pietro Rugolo, known as Pete Rugolo, was born in 1915 in San Piero Patti, Sicily. His family emigrated to the United States in 1920 and he grew up in Santa Rosa, California, where his father was a shoemaker. He began on the baritone horn, like his father, and quickly switched to other instruments, above all French horn and piano. He studied composition with Darius Milhaud at Mills College in Oakland and then became arranger and composer for the guitarist and bandleader Johnny Richards. During the Second World War he played in an army band with the alto saxophonist Paul Desmond.

After the war he worked for Stan Kenton. Together with the songwriter Joe Greene he made songs that helped make Kenton's band one of the most popular in America. In the 1950s he wrote arrangements for pop and jazz singers, above all for June Christy, on albums such as Something Cool. He worked on film musicals at MGM and in the late 1950s was A&R director at Capitol Records. His arrangements for The Four Freshmen and Five Trombones brought that group to the attention of jazz lovers.

In the 1960s and 1970s he wrote a great deal of music for television, including for Leave It to Beaver, Thriller, The Fugitive and Alias Smith and Jones. For The Fugitive he wrote ninety minutes of music, covering, among other things, suspense, love themes and chases. He also composed for films such as Jack the Ripper (1959) and The Sweet Ride (1968). Rugolo died in 2011.
artiest/pete-rugolo.listen: Listen to a track by June Christy from the album Something Cool, arranged by Rugolo. Notice how the accompaniment is arranged around her voice.

artiest/pete-townshend.text:
Pete Townshend is an English guitarist and songwriter, the founder and main writer of The Who. He was born in 1945 in Chiswick, in west London. His father played saxophone in an air force dance orchestra, his mother was a singer. In 1956 he saw the film Rock Around the Clock and then Bill Haley in concert. That year he got his first guitar and taught himself to play, without ever learning to read music. With his school friend John Entwistle he joined Roger Daltrey's Detours. After the arrival of the drummer Keith Moon, from 1964 that band was called The Who.

Townshend wrote the first hits, such as I Can't Explain and, in 1965, My Generation, an angry song for a generation of young people. He was one of the first to experiment with feedback from his amplifier. On stage he swung his arm like a windmill across the strings, and after he accidentally broke his guitar against the ceiling in 1964, smashing instruments became a regular part of the shows. With I Can See for Miles (1967), The Who had their biggest hit in America.

Townshend wanted more than separate singles. He wrote the rock operas Tommy (1969) and Quadrophenia (1973) and the album Who's Next (1971). He also made solo records such as Empty Glass (1980). He also plays keyboards, synthesizer, mandolin and many other instruments, all self-taught. His hard playing and his ambition to tell big stories with rock made him one of the most influential figures of the 1960s and 1970s.
artiest/pete-townshend.listen: Listen to My Generation by The Who. Notice the stuttering vocals, Townshend's fierce guitar chords and the ending in which the band gets ever louder and wilder.

artiest/pete-waterman.text:
Pete Waterman is an English producer, songwriter and television personality. He was born in 1947 in Coventry and after school worked as a fireman on steam locomotives. Inspired by the Beatles he then chose music. He collected rare American records and became a DJ with a mix of rhythm and blues and soul. At the Locarno club in Coventry he played afternoon discos for young people under eighteen. There he noticed that young dancers loved fast records, something he never forgot. He then worked for record companies, including in Philadelphia and in Jamaica with Peter Tosh and Lee Perry.

In 1984 he started his own company PWL and brought in the producers Mike Stock and Matt Aitken. This is how Stock Aitken Waterman came about, the most successful production team of the British 1980s. Waterman was the man with the ear for what the public wanted and the business side, while Stock and Aitken worked the songs out in the studio. From their studio in the Borough they made hits for Dead or Alive, Bananarama, Mel and Kim, Rick Astley, Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan. Their sound was fast, tight and electronic, with choruses you could sing along to straight away, exactly what the dancers at the Locarno had always wanted.

Waterman was involved in at least twenty-two British number 1 hits, later also with the group Steps. On television he presented The Hit Man and Her and sat on the jury of Pop Idol. He is also a great railway enthusiast with his own collection of locomotives.
artiest/pete-waterman.listen: Listen to Rick Astley's Never Gonna Give You Up from 1987. Notice the fast tempo, the pumping synthesizer bass and Astley's deep voice, which you would not expect on a dance record like this.

artiest/peter-baumann.text:
Peter Baumann was born in 1953 in West Berlin, the son of a composer and an actress. When he was eight, the Berlin Wall was built. He attended the American/German Community School, where he learned English and first came into contact with American culture. At fourteen he played in a cover band in clubs for American soldiers. In 1971, aged eighteen, he met Christopher Franke and became a member of Tangerine Dream, succeeding the organist Steve Schroyder. With Edgar Froese and Franke he formed the core of the German electronic group.

Two years later Tangerine Dream signed with Virgin Records. The first album there, Phaedra, reached the top ten in the Melody Maker charts. The group then toured the world for eight years and wrote music for a few films. Baumann left the group temporarily in 1973 and 1975, and permanently in 1977, shortly after the first American tour. In 1976 he had composed his first solo album Romance 76 while still touring with the band.

In the 1980s he founded the label Private Music, which released instrumental albums that were often regarded as new age, including by Yanni, Patrick O'Hearn, Suzanne Ciani and his old bandmates Tangerine Dream. He also released albums himself, such as Trans Harmonic Nights (1979) and Strangers in the Night (1983). Since the beginning of this century he has focused on science and philosophy concerning the human condition.
artiest/peter-baumann.listen: Listen to Phaedra by Tangerine Dream. Notice the electronic sounds and how they carry the music.

artiest/peter-brotzmann.text: Peter Brötzmann, from Wuppertal, studied fine art and worked for the Fluxus artist Nam June Paik. He taught himself to play saxophone and clarinet. The free jazz of Albert Ayler and Ornette Coleman showed him the way. In 1968 he recorded Machine Gun with eight musicians, among them Han Bennink and Willem Breuker: one of the loudest and most violent jazz records ever, often seen as the sound of European free jazz. In 1969 he co-founded the label FMP in Berlin with others. Until his death in 2023 he performed all over the world, often with young musicians.
artiest/peter-brotzmann.listen: Hear the power of the saxophones: a wall of sound instead of a melody.

artiest/peter-buck.text:
Peter Buck was born in 1956 in Berkeley, California, and is an American musician and songwriter. He grew up in, among other places, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Atlanta. He studied briefly at Emory University and moved to Athens, Georgia, where he studied at the University of Georgia. There he worked at the record shop Wuxtry Records. In that shop he met Michael Stipe, the future singer of R.E.M., and Bertis Downs, the band's future manager.

Buck was a co-founder and the guitarist of the alternative rock band R.E.M. In those years, from 1980 to 2011, he also played banjo and mandolin on a few songs. Besides R.E.M. he played in many side projects, including Hindu Love Gods, The Minus 5, Tuatara, The Baseball Project, Robyn Hitchcock and the Venus 3, Tired Pony, Filthy Friends and Arthur Buck, with Joseph Arthur. He has also been a producer for, among others, Uncle Tupelo, The Feelies and The Jayhawks. He also played as a session musician for The Replacements, Billy Bragg and the Decemberists.

After the end of R.E.M. he began a solo career, with Peter Buck (2012), I Am Back to Blow Your Mind Once Again (2014) and Warzone Earth (2015). For the live presentation of his solo album he formed the band Richard M. Nixon, which never released an official record.
artiest/peter-buck.listen: Listen to an R.E.M. song and notice Buck's guitar. Try to hear what role the guitar plays in the whole.

artiest/peter-en-zijn-rockets.text:
Peter en zijn Rockets, in English Peter and his Rockets, was the band of Peter Koelewijn from Eindhoven. Koelewijn began on guitar at thirteen and from 1957 wrote his first songs, still in English. He started his first band at secondary school with the guitarists Karel Jansen and Roelof Egmond and the singer Anneke Grönloh; later Harry van Hoof, the future conductor, and the drummer Peter van der Voort joined. In 1959 the saxophonist Klaus Buchholz and the bassist Karel Jansen joined the group.

In December 1959 the band recorded Kom van dat dak af for Bovema. The combination of American rock 'n' roll and Dutch lyrics was remarkably innovative at the time. In May 1960 it became a big success in the Netherlands and Belgium. The Rockets signed with Philips, but the follow-ups Laat Me Los and Marijke did less well. In 1967 Koelewijn disbanded the group to write and produce songs for others, and to present radio programmes.

In 1970 he brought the Rockets together again for a glam rock period that lasted five years. In 1981 he brought in musicians from the band Bunny for a new line-up, which lasted until 1997. Its first album was the live album Peter Live, from which Kom van dat dak af and Klap maar in je handen reached the charts. The group stands for the beginning of Dutch-language rock 'n' roll.
artiest/peter-en-zijn-rockets.listen: Listen to Kom van dat dak af. Notice how American rock 'n' roll and Dutch vocals come together, and how the saxophone joins in with the band.

artiest/peter-frampton.text:
Peter Frampton was born in 1950 in Beckenham, Kent. His father was an art teacher at his school. At seven he found his grandmother's banjolele in the attic, on which he taught himself to play. Later he taught himself guitar and piano, and at eight he began classical lessons. He was influenced by Cliff Richard and the Shadows, Buddy Holly, Eddie Cochran, the Ventures, Jimi Hendrix and the Beatles, and his father played him records by the Gypsy jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt.

Frampton became known as a member of the rock bands The Herd and Humble Pie. He then achieved great success as a solo artist. His breakthrough was the 1976 live album Frampton Comes Alive!, the best-selling album of that year in the United States, with several hit singles. His best-known songs are Show Me the Way, Baby, I Love Your Way, Do You Feel Like We Do and I'm in You, which can still be heard on classic rock radio. Earlier solo albums include Wind of Change (1972) and Frampton (1975).

He has worked with Ringo Starr, John Entwistle of The Who, David Bowie, Joe Bonamassa and with Matt Cameron and Mike McCready of Pearl Jam. He appeared as himself in television series such as The Simpsons and Family Guy. In 2024 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/peter-frampton.listen: Listen to Do You Feel Like We Do from Frampton Comes Alive!. Notice the guitar and how alive the recording sounds.

artiest/peter-gabriel.text:
Peter Gabriel is an English singer, songwriter and human rights activist, born in 1950 in Chobham, Surrey. At the boarding school Charterhouse he founded Genesis in 1967 with fellow pupils. For eight years he was the group's singer and main lyricist, and he stood out for his theatrical performances and costumes, such as a fox outfit in 1972. In 1975, after the tour for The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway, he left; the drummer Phil Collins became the new singer.

Between 1977 and 1982 Gabriel made four solo albums that are all called Peter Gabriel and can be told apart only by the sleeve. They blend prog rock, new wave and post-punk with music from other parts of the world. Well-known songs include Solsbury Hill, Games Without Frontiers, Shock the Monkey and Biko, a protest song against apartheid. During the recording of Intruder, on the third album, gated reverb came about, a sharply truncated reverb on the drums, which he made famous. On the fourth album he used the Fairlight, one of the first digital samplers, which was so expensive that only stars could afford it.

The album So (1986) became his greatest success. The single Sledgehammer reached number 1 in America and its video won nine MTV Video Music Awards. In 1982 Gabriel co-founded the world music festival WOMAD, and later he started Real World Studios and Real World Records, giving musicians from all over the world a platform. He was inducted twice into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, with Genesis and as a solo artist. In 2023 i/o was released.
artiest/peter-gabriel.listen: Listen to the start of Intruder: Phil Collins's drums sound hard and short, as if the reverb is abruptly cut off. That is the gated reverb. Notice that you hear no cymbals in this song, which makes that drum sound stand out even more.

artiest/peter-hook.text:
Peter Hook was born in 1956 in Salford, near Manchester. His nickname Hooky comes from his stepfather's surname. In 1976 he saw the Sex Pistols in Manchester with his childhood friend Bernard Sumner. He borrowed thirty-five pounds from his mother, bought his first bass guitar and formed a band with Sumner and Terry Mason. It was first called Warsaw and from January 1978 played under the name Joy Division.

Hook used the bass guitar as a lead instrument. He played melodies on the high strings and gave his bass a heavy chorus effect, a sound by which you recognise him immediately. After the death of the singer Ian Curtis in 1980, the remaining members carried on as New Order. Hook played there until 2007. In the 1980s he also produced records by Inspiral Carpets and the Stone Roses. Outside his main bands he made music with Revenge, Freebass and above all Monaco, who had a club hit in 1997 with What Do You Want From Me?. Later he performed with Peter Hook & the Light and made Haçienda Classiçal (2016).

For pop history, Hook is important as one of the faces of the Manchester scene around the label Factory. The course mentions him in a story about the money Factory lost, in which he gave his own estimate. It shows that he was not only a bassist, but also a witness with an opinion of his own about the label. In 2026 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Joy Division and New Order.
artiest/peter-hook.listen: Listen to a Joy Division or New Order song and follow only the bass guitar. Notice how often Hook plays the melody high on the strings, instead of low beneath the rest.

artiest/peter-koelewijn.text:
Peter Koelewijn was born in 1940 in Eindhoven, the son of a fishmonger. He got his first guitar at thirteen and from 1957 wrote songs, at first in English. He is regarded as one of the founders of Dutch-language rock 'n' roll. With his band Peter and his Rockets he recorded Kom van dat dak af in December 1959, which became a big success in the Netherlands and Belgium in May 1960. That combination of American rock 'n' roll and Dutch lyrics was very innovative at the time. His next singles Laat Me Los and Marijke did less well. In 1967 he disbanded the Rockets to write and produce songs for other artists, and to make radio programmes.

In 1970 he brought the band together again for a glam rock period of five years. His composition Klap Maar in Je Handen from 1973 became a number one for the South African singer Maria, and is still played at parties there. In 1977 his first solo album Het Beste in Mij Is Niet Goed Genoeg Voor Jou appeared, containing, among others, KL 204 (Als Ik God Was), of which Engelbert Humperdinck recorded an English version.

In 1981 he formed a new line-up of the Rockets with musicians from the band Bunny, which lasted until 1997. In 1985 he had a top 40 hit with Sprong in Het Duister. In 1995 he fronted the comedy band Gompie, whose version of Smokie's Living Next Door to Alice topped the charts. Koelewijn is thus a singer as well as a songwriter and producer, and an important name in Dutch-language pop music.
artiest/peter-koelewijn.listen: Listen to Kom van dat dak af. Notice how Dutch lyrics and the rock 'n' roll sound work together and what made that new in 1960.

artiest/peter-kowald.text:
Peter Kowald was born in 1944 and was a German bassist and tuba player from free jazz and free improvisation. He was a member of the Globe Unity Orchestra and, until 1985, of the London Jazz Composer's Orchestra, and toured as a solo double bassist. He worked with many European and American free jazz musicians, among them Peter Brötzmann, Irène Schweizer, Fred Anderson, Hamid Drake, Wadada Leo Smith, William Parker, Barre Phillips, Joëlle Léandre and Evan Parker. He also recorded solo albums for double bass and made special duos with, among others, Maarten Altena, Barry Guy and Joëlle Léandre.

Kowald also collaborated a great deal with poets, visual artists and dancers. Examples are Die Klage der Kaiserin from 1989 with Pina Bausch, short pieces with Jean Sasportes and performances with Min Tanaka and Butch Morris. He also worked in duo with singers such as Jeanne Lee, Diamanda Galás and Sainkho Namtchylak. His albums include Hot Lotta (1973), Carpathes (1976), Touch the Earth (1980) and Global Village Suite Improvised (1988).

His special interest lay with Global Village, an international improvisation ensemble with musicians from China, Japan, the Near East, southern Europe and North and South America. Kowald died in 2002 in New York of a heart attack.
artiest/peter-kowald.listen: Listen to a duo by Kowald, for example with Joëlle Léandre or Barre Phillips. Notice how two double basses talk to each other, with no fixed rhythm.
